name: line-finder measures the rectangle, label-crop crops it as-is
info:
One `line-finder` with four regions named `left`, `right`, `top` and
`bottom` reports the rectangle they bound in `msg.lineFinder.rect` -
corners, centre, size and angle in full-frame pixels. A `label-crop` with
**Boundary = From line-finder** detects nothing itself: it takes that
rectangle off the message and deskews and crops to it, so the tuning
lives in one place (the line-finder, which can draw its regions on the
last frame it saw and run them from its editor) and what it draws on the
flow canvas is exactly what gets cropped.

The frame here is synthetic so the example runs on import: the function
node draws a pale 480x312 label tilted 4 degrees on a dark 800x600 tray.
Replace it with your camera or file-in node and re-aim the four regions
in the line-finder's editor (**Add rectangle** lays them out, **Run on
this image** shows what each one found).

If the line-finder misses an edge the frame is NOT cropped:
`msg.labelCrop.reason` is `upstream-rect:missing-edge:top` (the finder's
own reason), `msg.labelCrop.detected` is false and the payload passes
through unchanged. `msg.lineFinder.lines` is still on the message, so the
region to re-aim is in the debug sidebar already. A message with no
rectangle at all is `no-upstream-rect`; a malformed one is
`bad-upstream-rect`.

The blob gates (`aspectRatio`, `expectedSizeFraction`, `minConfidence`,
...) do not apply in this mode, as they do not in calipers mode;
`cropMargin`, `minRotateAngleDeg` and the output format do.
